title: Looking for thoughts on...The Saltwind Colonies
author: Lanky_Ad_1973
selftext:
Hey Gang,

Claude has enabled me to live the dream of combining all the best bits of the early city sim builders of the late 90's early 2000's. I am having a blast and feel like the pre-alpha is in a place when i can show you guys, invite critique and share any idea or thoughts you might have for improvements.

I am looking forward to getting a test release out so people can have a real go on it. 

Claude Opus doing most of the heavy lifting with Fable used for management and some Sonnet, blender for basic 3D models over which Chat GPT paints the artwork.

Subscriptions

Claude Max 100  
Chat GPT Pro   
Sumo Pro for a month

comments.author: Significant-Neck-520
comments.body: Looking really nice. The only thing I missed for some reason was the shore bring animated, never tought it would be that important but it feels like it is missing. I understand that would be a pain to implement though. I do think the graphics look solid tough, nice work!

replies.author: Lanky_Ad_1973
replies.body: much obliged bud! and you raise a good point about the shore it feels a touch pond like :)

comments.author: maarkeez
comments.body:
Pharaoh: a new era vibes with age of empires look and feel. Love it!!

Just out of interest, I'd say the subscription costs about €250 a month, just for the AI. How fast is it? I'm just wondering whether it's worth it. Are you planning to monetise it?

I was also thinking of building my own game using just Claude Pro. I've had a look at the limits, and I reckon I'll hit them pretty quickly.

At the moment, I'm slowly working on it with a local llama and Qwen 3.8, but because my Mac only has 32GB of RAM, this is a very slow solution. Most of my workflow involves writing a detailed, big plan and keeping it running over night. So I checked the results after in the morning (it's a pet project).

replies.author: Lanky_Ad_1973
replies.body:
ITs 120 euros a month all in for me.   
I made the leap to base level Max after trying for a while on Pro, but at the rate i want to go i kept hitting the limit. with the 5X i have yet to hit one, and Claude gifted me $250 of Claude Cloud to try which was also very useful for deep soak runs of the game

I found it very useful to get it to create the tools for changing parameters along the way. that way i can make manual fine tuning to say, shadows, without wasting tokens

replies.author: maarkeez
replies.body: Thanks for the context!!

for art style, tell it to go out and research the graphical levels of the time with particular images or bit you remember vividly and screenshots.  
one tip, the desired resolution is lower than you think. your childhood i imagination fills in more details than trying to cram in fine detail into the models

replies.author: Lanky_Ad_1973
replies.body:
after trial and error:

Opus creates a basic 3D model of simple shapes, over which chatgpt painted my requested building. It has a art loop which it applies to all new art to knock back the saturation and crispness to the level i want in the game. 

This is especially useful for the animation sheets. GPT couldn't hold consistency on its own.

comments.author: This-Way-5162
comments.body: How do you create the models/sprites for the characters?

replies.author: Lanky_Ad_1973
replies.body:
I dialed in an Art Loop in Claude that it runs to generate a prompt for Chat GPT to action, this same loop then also validates the art for a number of different criteria.   
Claude MCPs into the free version of blender on my pc to generate a basic 3D rendering of what i am trying to achieve. this is then given to GPT as it is way better at painting over 3D model than it is at rendering the exact same item from different angles.  
Claude then takes the artwork, chops,shears, desaturates, derezzes it to much the game style and boom!  
Most of the time.

Shader rendering still sucks, so i got it to make me a shader engine and i hand paint them.
